163	    return { inputTokens: this.inputTokens, outputTokens: this.outputTokens }
164	  }
165	
166	  /**
167	   * The refusal that keeps a cell out of the runner.
168	   * @param cell - the cell about to start.
169	   * @returns the error to record for the cell, or `undefined` when nothing refuses it.
170	   */
171	  refusal(cell: FleetCell): FleetCellError | undefined {
172	    const spent = this.inputTokens + this.outputTokens
173	    if (this.ceiling !== undefined && spent >= this.ceiling) {
174	      return {
175	        code: 'FLEET_TOKEN_CEILING_REACHED' satisfies FleetCellErrorCode,
176	        message: `the plan's token ceiling of ${this.ceiling} was reached at ${spent} tokens`,
177	      }
178	    }
179	    const errors = this.consecutiveErrors.get(routeName(cell.model)) ?? 0
180	    if (this.breaker !== undefined && errors >= this.breaker.consecutiveErrors) {
181	      return {
182	        code: 'FLEET_ROUTE_BREAKER_OPEN' satisfies FleetCellErrorCode,
183	        message: `route ${routeName(cell.model)} stopped after ${errors} consecutive errors`,
184	      }
185	    }
186	    return undefined
187	  }
188	
189	  /**
190	   * Fold one outcome the runner produced. A refused cell never reaches this,
191	   * so a refusal neither opens another route's breaker nor moves the spend.
192	   * @param outcome - the settled outcome of one cell the runner handled.
193	   */
194	  record(outcome: FleetCellOutcome): void {
195	    const route = routeName(outcome.cell.model)
196	    if ('error' in outcome) {
197	      this.consecutiveErrors.set(route, (this.consecutiveErrors.get(route) ?? 0) + 1)
198	      return
199	    }
200	    this.consecutiveErrors.set(route, 0)
201	    this.inputTokens += outcome.report.usage?.inputTokens ?? 0
202	    this.outputTokens += outcome.report.usage?.outputTokens ?? 0
203	  }
204	}

206	/** Key of the leaderboard row a cell belongs to. */
207	function rowKey(cell: FleetCell): string {
208	  return `${cell.model.provider}\0${cell.model.model}\0${cell.environment}`
209	}

211	/**
212	 * Keep the enumerated cells a plan named, in plan order.
213	 * @throws {@link FleetError} when the selection is empty or names a cell the
214	 *   plan's environments, routes, and repetition count do not enumerate.
215	 */
216	function restrict(enumerated: readonly FleetCell[], selected: readonly FleetCell[]): FleetCell[] {
217	  if (selected.length === 0) throw new FleetError('the plan names no cell to run', 'FLEET_INVALID_PLAN')
218	  const wanted = new Set(selected.map(fleetCellKey))
219	  const kept = enumerated.filter(cell => wanted.has(fleetCellKey(cell)))
220	  for (const key of kept.map(fleetCellKey)) wanted.delete(key)
221	  const unenumerated = [...wanted]
222	  if (unenumerated.length > 0) {
223	    throw new FleetError(`cell "${unenumerated[0] as string}" is not one this plan enumerates`, 'FLEET_INVALID_PLAN')
224	  }
225	  return kept
226	}
227	
228	/**
229	 * Identity of one cell inside its batch. Two cells with the same key are the
230	 * same unit of the same plan, so a driver indexing cells across processes —
231	 * against a ledger or against the run stamps already in the session logs —
232	 * keys them by this instead of comparing the records field by field.
233	 * @param cell - the cell to name.
234	 * @returns the key, unique inside one plan.
235	 */
236	export function fleetCellKey(cell: FleetCell): string {
237	  return `${cell.environment} ${cell.model.provider}/${cell.model.model} ${cell.repetition}`
238	}
239	
240	/** Fold the leaderboard from the cell outcomes, one row per model route and environment. */
241	function foldLeaderboard(
242	  outcomes: readonly FleetCellOutcome[],
243	  definitions: ReadonlyMap<EnvironmentId, EnvironmentDefinition>,
244	): LeaderboardRow[] {
245	  const rows = new Map<string, LeaderboardRow>()
246	  for (const outcome of outcomes) {
247	    const key = rowKey(outcome.cell)
248	    const definition = definitions.get(outcome.cell.environment) as EnvironmentDefinition
249	    const row = rows.get(key) ?? {
250	      provider: outcome.cell.model.provider,
251	      model: outcome.cell.model.model,
252	      environmentId: outcome.cell.environment,
253	      environmentKind: definition.kind,
254	      heldOut: definition.heldOut,
255	      runs: 0,
256	      errors: 0,
257	      certified: 0,
258	      certificateRate: 0,
259	      attemptsMean: 0,
260	      inputTokens: 0,
261	      outputTokens: 0,
262	    }
263	    rows.set(key, 'report' in outcome ? withReport(row, outcome.report) : { ...row, errors: row.errors + 1 })
264	  }
265	  return [...rows.values()]
266	}
267	
268	/** Add one report to a row, recomputing the derived rates. */
269	function withReport(row: LeaderboardRow, report: EnvironmentRunReport): LeaderboardRow {
270	  const runs = row.runs + 1
271	  const certified = row.certified + (report.certified ? 1 : 0)
272	  const attempts = row.attemptsMean * row.runs + report.attempts.length
273	  return {
274	    ...row,
275	    ...report.stamp.ladder === undefined ? {} : { ladder: report.stamp.ladder },
276	    isolation: report.stamp.isolation,
277	    implementer: report.stamp.implementer ?? ROUTE_IMPLEMENTER,
278	    runs,
279	    certified,
280	    certificateRate: certified / runs,
281	    attemptsMean: attempts / runs,
282	    inputTokens: row.inputTokens + (report.usage?.inputTokens ?? 0),
283	    outputTokens: row.outputTokens + (report.usage?.outputTokens ?? 0),
284	  }
285	}

287	/**
288	 * Render a leaderboard as a Markdown table for people; the report stays the record.
289	 * @param report - a fleet run report.
290	 * @returns one table with a header row and one row per leaderboard entry.
291	 */
292	export function leaderboardMarkdown(report: FleetRunReport): string {
293	  const header = '| Model | Ladder | Implementer | Environment | Held out | Isolation | Runs | Errors | Certified | Rate | Attempts | Tokens in / out |'
294	  const rule = '|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|'
295	  const lines = report.leaderboard.map(row => (
296	    `| ${row.provider}/${row.model} | ${ladderCell(row.ladder)} | ${row.implementer ?? '-'} | ${row.environmentId} | ${row.heldOut ? 'yes' : 'no'} | ${row.isolation ?? '-'} | ${row.runs} | ${row.errors} | ${row.certified} | ${row.certificateRate.toFixed(2)} | ${row.attemptsMean.toFixed(2)} | ${row.inputTokens} / ${row.outputTokens} |`
297	  ))
298	  return [`Fleet run \`${report.group}\``, '', header, rule, ...lines].join('\n') + '\n'
299	}
300	
301	/** One row's ladder as its Markdown cell: the rungs in attempt order, or the dash of a row that ran none. */
302	function ladderCell(ladder: readonly EnvironmentRunModel[] | undefined): string {
303	  return ladder === undefined ? '-' : ladder.map(routeName).join(' > ')
304	}

306	/** Fleet runs (`ctx.fleet`): a plan of environment cells through the runner, with a leaderboard. */
307	export class FleetService extends Service {
308	  static inject = ['environments', 'environmentRuns', 'agentDefaultModel']
309	
310	  static Config: z<Config> = z.object({
311	    maxConcurrent: z.natural().min(1).default(1),
312	    // Prevent Schemastery from materializing an omitted routeBreaker as `{}`,
313	    // whose missing `consecutiveErrors` would reject every breakerless deployment.
314	    routeBreaker: z.object({
315	      consecutiveErrors: z.natural().min(1).required(),
316	    }).default(undefined as unknown as RouteBreakerConfig),
317	    workspaceRetention: z.union(['keep', 'remove-certified', 'remove-all'] as const).required(),
318	  })
319	
320	  private readonly resolved: ResolvedConfig
321	
322	  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config) {
323	    super(ctx, 'fleet')
324	    this.resolved = resolveConfig(config)
325	  }
326	
327	  /**
328	   * Run every cell of a plan and fold the leaderboard. A cell whose run
329	   * throws is kept as an error outcome, as is a cell the route breaker or the
330	   * token ceiling refused to start; the fleet run itself rejects only for a
331	   * plan it cannot start.
332	   * @param plan - environments, model routes, an optional attempt ladder and
333	   *   implementer, repetitions, an optional exact cell selection, workspace
334	   *   root, group, district, policy version, base seed, token ceiling, and
335	   *   abort signal.
336	   * @returns every cell's outcome in plan order, the leaderboard folded from the reports, and the run's spend.
337	   * @throws {@link FleetError} when the plan selects no environment, asks for
338	   *   no repetition, names no or an unenumerated cell, sets a token ceiling
339	   *   that is not a positive integer, sets a seed that is not a safe
340	   *   non-negative integer, or carries an attempt ladder with no rung.
341	   */
342	  async run(plan: FleetPlan): Promise<FleetRunReport> {
343	    if (!Number.isInteger(plan.repetitions) || plan.repetitions < 1) {
344	      throw new FleetError(`repetitions must be a positive integer, got ${String(plan.repetitions)}`, 'FLEET_INVALID_PLAN')
345	    }
346	    if (plan.tokenCeiling !== undefined && (!Number.isInteger(plan.tokenCeiling) || plan.tokenCeiling < 1)) {
347	      throw new FleetError(`tokenCeiling must be a positive integer, got ${String(plan.tokenCeiling)}`, 'FLEET_INVALID_PLAN')
348	    }
349	    // The base seed is refused here rather than per cell: it is arithmetic the
350	    // fleet performs, so a bad base would otherwise surface as every cell failing.
351	    if (plan.seed !== undefined && !isSeed(plan.seed)) {
352	      throw new FleetError(`seed must be a non-negative integer, got ${String(plan.seed)}`, 'FLEET_INVALID_PLAN')
353	    }
354	    // An empty ladder is the whole plan's, so it is refused once here instead of
355	    // once per cell; the runner still owns the rung ceiling, which is its config.
356	    if (plan.ladder !== undefined && plan.ladder.length === 0) {
357	      throw new FleetError('the plan\'s attempt ladder names no rung', 'FLEET_INVALID_PLAN')
358	    }
359	    const definitions = this.select(plan)
360	    if (definitions.size === 0) throw new FleetError('the plan selects no environment', 'FLEET_EMPTY_PLAN')
361	    const models = plan.models.length === 0 ? [this.defaultModel()] : plan.models
362	    const group = plan.group ?? `fleet-${randomUUID()}`
363	    const enumerated: FleetCell[] = []
364	    for (const environment of definitions.keys()) {
365	      for (const model of models) {
366	        for (let repetition = 0; repetition < plan.repetitions; repetition += 1) enumerated.push({ environment, model, repetition })
367	      }
368	    }
369	    const cells = plan.cells === undefined ? enumerated : restrict(enumerated, plan.cells)
370	    const ledger = new PlanLedger(this.resolved.routeBreaker, plan.tokenCeiling)
371	    const tasks = cells.map(cell => () => this.runCell(cell, plan, group, ledger))
372	    const outcomes = await bounded(tasks, this.resolved.maxConcurrent)
373	    return { group, cells: outcomes, leaderboard: foldLeaderboard(outcomes, definitions), spend: ledger.spend }
374	  }
375	
376	  /** Resolve the plan's environment selection against the registry, in registry order. */
377	  private select(plan: FleetPlan): Map<EnvironmentId, EnvironmentDefinition> {
378	    const selected = 'ids' in plan.environments
379	      ? plan.environments.ids.flatMap((id) => {
380	        const definition = this.ctx.environments.get(id)
381	        if (definition === undefined) throw new FleetError(`environment "${id}" is not registered`, 'FLEET_INVALID_PLAN')
382	        return [definition]
383	      })
384	      : this.ctx.environments.list(plan.environments.filter)
385	    return new Map(selected.map(definition => [definition.id, definition]))
386	  }
387	
388	  /** The composition's default model route, detached from the selection service. */
389	  private defaultModel(): EnvironmentRunModel {
390	    const selection = this.ctx.agentDefaultModel.currentSelection()
391	    return { provider: selection.provider, model: selection.model }
392	  }
393	
394	  /**
395	   * Run one cell unless the ledger refuses it, fold the outcome back into the
396	   * ledger, and apply the configured workspace retention.
397	   */
398	  private async runCell(cell: FleetCell, plan: FleetPlan, group: string, ledger: PlanLedger): Promise<FleetCellOutcome> {
399	    const refusal = ledger.refusal(cell)
400	    if (refusal !== undefined) return this.settle({ cell, error: refusal }, plan, group)
401	    const { outcome, workspace } = await this.execute(cell, plan, group)
402	    ledger.record(outcome)
403	    if (workspace !== undefined && this.removes(outcome)) await rm(workspace, { recursive: true, force: true })
404	    return this.settle(outcome, plan, group)
405	  }
406	
407	  /** Announce one settled cell after its workspace retention has run. */
408	  private settle(outcome: FleetCellOutcome, plan: FleetPlan, group: string): FleetCellOutcome {
409	    const payload: FleetCellEvent = {
410	      group,
411	      ...plan.district === undefined ? {} : { district: plan.district },
412	      cell: outcome.cell,
413	      outcome: 'report' in outcome
414	        ? { kind: 'reported', sessionId: outcome.report.sessionId, certified: outcome.report.certified }
415	        : { kind: 'error', ...outcome.error.code === undefined ? {} : { code: outcome.error.code }, message: outcome.error.message },
416	    }
417	    this.ctx.emit('fleet/cell', payload)
418	    return outcome
419	  }
420	
421	  /** Whether the configured retention removes the workspace of a settled cell. */
422	  private removes(outcome: FleetCellOutcome): boolean {
423	    const retention = this.resolved.workspaceRetention
424	    switch (retention) {
425	      case 'keep': return false
426	      case 'remove-certified': return 'report' in outcome && outcome.report.certified
427	      case 'remove-all': return true
428	      default: return assertNever(retention, 'workspace retention')
429	    }
430	  }
431	
432	  /**
433	   * Run one cell in a fresh workspace directory; a thrown error becomes the
434	   * cell's outcome. The workspace is returned when one was minted, so retention
435	   * can reach a directory whose run then failed.
436	   */
437	  private async execute(
438	    cell: FleetCell,
439	    plan: FleetPlan,
440	    group: string,
441	  ): Promise<{ outcome: FleetCellOutcome; workspace?: string }> {
442	    let workspace: string | undefined
443	    try {
444	      workspace = await mkdtemp(join(plan.workspaceRoot, 'cell-'))
445	      const report = await this.ctx.environmentRuns.run({
446	        environment: cell.environment,
447	        workspace,
448	        model: cell.model,
449	        ...plan.ladder === undefined ? {} : { ladder: plan.ladder },
450	        ...plan.implementer === undefined ? {} : { implementer: plan.implementer },
451	        repetition: cell.repetition,
452	        group,
453	        ...plan.district === undefined ? {} : { district: plan.district },
454	        ...plan.policyVersion === undefined ? {} : { policyVersion: plan.policyVersion },
455	        ...plan.seed === undefined ? {} : { seed: plan.seed + cell.repetition },
456	        ...plan.signal === undefined ? {} : { signal: plan.signal },
457	      })
458	      return { outcome: { cell, report }, workspace }
459	    } catch (error: unknown) {
460	      const outcome: FleetCellOutcome = { cell, error: cellError(error) }
461	      return workspace === undefined ? { outcome } : { outcome, workspace }
462	    }
463	  }
464	}
465	
466	export default FleetService

148	  /**
149	   * Freeze a plan, run both arms through the fleet at the same repetition
150	   * indexes, and fold the paired comparison. Every refusal happens before the
151	   * first cell runs; a cell the fleet kept as an error leaves its repetition
152	   * unpaired instead of failing the experiment.
153	   * @param plan - environments, repetitions, the two arms with their model
154	   *   routes and optional attempt ladders and implementers, the workspace root,
155	   *   and an optional policy version, base seed, frozen digest, abort signal,
156	   *   and result sink.
157	   * @returns the digest, both arms with their ladders and stamp groups, one
158	   *   cell per environment, the pooled delta with its interval, the spend, the
159	   *   caps both arms ran under, and the verdict.
160	   * @throws {@link ExperimentError} for a plan that names no or a duplicate or
161	   *   unregistered environment, asks for no repetition, sets a seed that is not
162	   *   a safe non-negative integer, carries an arm ladder with no rung or one
163	   *   whose first rung names another route, whose two arms would run under
164	   *   different caps, declares a digest its content does not freeze to, or
165	   *   projects more tokens than the budget.
166	   */
167	  async run(plan: ExperimentPlan): Promise<ExperimentResult> {
168	    const { digest, caps } = this.freeze(plan)
169	    const arms: ExperimentArms = {
170	      baseline: resolveArm(plan.baseline, digest, 'baseline'),
171	      candidate: resolveArm(plan.candidate, digest, 'candidate'),
172	    }
173	    const baseline = await this.runArm(plan, arms.baseline)
174	    const candidate = await this.runArm(plan, arms.candidate)
175	    const result = foldExperiment({
176	      digest,
177	      arms,
178	      environments: plan.environments,
179	      repetitions: plan.repetitions,
180	      thresholds: this.resolved.thresholds,

191	   * over them, and check the projection against the budget.
192	   */
193	  private freeze(plan: ExperimentPlan): { digest: string; caps: readonly BudgetCap[] } {
194	    if (!Number.isInteger(plan.repetitions) || plan.repetitions < 1) {
195	      throw new ExperimentError(`repetitions must be a positive integer, got ${String(plan.repetitions)}`, 'EXPERIMENT_INVALID_PLAN')
196	    }
197	    if (plan.seed !== undefined && !isSeed(plan.seed)) {
198	      throw new ExperimentError(`seed must be a non-negative integer, got ${String(plan.seed)}`, 'EXPERIMENT_INVALID_PLAN')
199	    }
200	    if (plan.environments.length === 0) throw new ExperimentError('the plan names no environment', 'EXPERIMENT_INVALID_PLAN')
201	    for (const role of EXPERIMENT_ARM_ROLES) {
202	      const arm = plan[role]
203	      if (arm.ladder?.length === 0) {
204	        throw new ExperimentError(`the ${role} arm's attempt ladder names no rung`, 'EXPERIMENT_INVALID_PLAN')
205	      }
206	      if (ladderConflicts(arm)) {
207	        const first = arm.ladder?.[0]?.model as EnvironmentRunModel
208	        throw new ExperimentError(`the ${role} arm runs ${arm.provider}/${arm.model} but its first ladder rung names ${first.provider}/${first.model}, so its first attempt would not be the arm it is published under`, 'EXPERIMENT_LADDER_CONFLICT')
209	      }
210	    }
211	    const named = new Set<EnvironmentId>()
212	    for (const environment of plan.environments) {
213	      if (named.has(environment)) throw new ExperimentError(`environment "${environment}" is named twice`, 'EXPERIMENT_INVALID_PLAN')
214	      if (this.ctx.environments.get(environment) === undefined) {
215	        throw new ExperimentError(`environment "${environment}" is not registered`, 'EXPERIMENT_INVALID_PLAN')
216	      }
217	      named.add(environment)
218	    }
219	    const caps = this.agreedCaps(plan)
220	    const digest = planDigest(plan, this.resolved.thresholds, caps)
221	    if (plan.digest !== undefined && plan.digest !== digest) {
222	      throw new ExperimentError(`the plan declares digest ${plan.digest} but freezes to ${digest}`, 'EXPERIMENT_PLAN_NOT_FROZEN')
223	    }
224	    const projected = projectedTokens(plan, this.resolved.thresholds.cellTokenCap)
225	    if (projected > this.resolved.tokenBudget) {
226	      throw new ExperimentError(`the plan projects ${projected} tokens over a budget of ${this.resolved.tokenBudget}`, 'EXPERIMENT_OVER_BUDGET')
227	    }
228	    return { digest, caps }
229	  }

235	   * @param plan - the frozen plan, supplying the implementer of each arm.

1	/**
2	 * Freezing one experiment plan: the content digest computed before any cell
3	 * runs, and the stamp `group` each arm's sessions carry so a later fold can
4	 * find them in the logs.
5	 *
6	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-experiments/plan
7	 */
8	
9	import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
10	import type { BudgetCap } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy'
11	import type { EnvironmentRunImplementer, EnvironmentRunRung } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner/types'
12	import { assertNever } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
13	import type { ExperimentArmPlan, ExperimentArmRole, ExperimentPlan, ExperimentThresholds } from './types.ts'
14	
15	/**
16	 * Group namespace this package owns. A `group` starting with it names an
17	 * experiment arm, so no other producer may mint one.
18	 */
19	export const EXPERIMENT_GROUP_PREFIX = 'experiment-'
20	
21	/** Self-declared version of the digested plan fields; a change to what they cover changes it. */
22	const EXPERIMENT_PLAN_VERSION = 5
23	
24	/** Arm roles in the order the digest and the runs take them. */
25	export const EXPERIMENT_ARM_ROLES: readonly ExperimentArmRole[] = ['baseline', 'candidate']
26	
27	const GROUP_PATTERN = new RegExp(`^${EXPERIMENT_GROUP_PREFIX}([0-9a-f]{64})-(${EXPERIMENT_ARM_ROLES.join('|')})$`)
28	
29	/**
30	 * The implementer one arm runs under.
31	 * @param arm - one arm as the plan names it.
32	 * @returns the named implementer, or the arm's own model route when it names none.
33	 */
34	export function armImplementer(arm: ExperimentArmPlan): EnvironmentRunImplementer {
35	  return arm.implementer ?? { kind: 'route' }
36	}
37	
38	/**
39	 * One implementer as the digest takes it: the discriminant, the subagent
40	 * provider, and its label, each in a fixed position, so the key order a caller
41	 * happened to write cannot change the digest.
42	 */
43	function digestedImplementer(implementer: EnvironmentRunImplementer): readonly (string | null)[] {
44	  switch (implementer.kind) {
45	    case 'route':
46	      return [implementer.kind, null, null]
47	    case 'subagent':
48	      return [implementer.kind, implementer.provider, implementer.label ?? null]
49	    /* v8 ignore next 2 -- EnvironmentRunImplementer is closed and every member is handled above */
50	    default:
51	      return assertNever(implementer, 'arm implementer')
52	  }
53	}
54	
55	/**
56	 * One arm's attempt ladder as the digest takes it: the model of each rung in
57	 * attempt order, with `null` for a rung that names none and therefore runs the
58	 * arm's own route. Two arms that ladder differently measure different routing,
59	 * so the rungs are part of what the digest freezes.
60	 */
61	function digestedLadder(ladder: readonly EnvironmentRunRung[] | undefined): readonly (readonly string[] | null)[] | null {
62	  if (ladder === undefined) return null
63	  return ladder.map(rung => (rung.model === undefined ? null : [rung.model.provider, rung.model.model]))
64	}
65	
66	/**
67	 * Whether one arm's first rung names a route other than the arm's own. The arm
68	 * is what a result and every scoreboard row are published under, so a first
69	 * rung naming another route would publish the arm's identity over an attempt it
70	 * never ran.
71	 * @param arm - one arm as the plan names it.
72	 * @returns `true` when the arm ladders and its first rung names another route.
73	 */
74	export function ladderConflicts(arm: ExperimentArmPlan): boolean {
75	  const first = arm.ladder?.[0]?.model
76	  if (first === undefined) return false
77	  return first.provider !== arm.provider || first.model !== arm.model
78	}
79	
80	/**
81	 * Content digest of the fields that decide what an experiment measures: the
82	 * two arms in role order, each with its model route, its attempt ladder, and
83	 * its implementer, the environment ids sorted so a caller's listing order
84	 * cannot change the identity, the repetition count, the policy version and base
85	 * seed both arms ran under, the thresholds, and the caps every cell of both
86	 * arms ran under.
87	 * The caps are digested because a cell cut off at one wall or token ceiling
88	 * measures something different from the same cell cut off at another, so two
89	 * comparisons run under different budgets are two experiments. The deployment's
90	 * token budget stays absent: it bounds what a deployment pays for across plans,
91	 * not what one comparison measures. The policy version and the seed are present
92	 * because both arms' sessions are found in the logs by the groups this digest
93	 * mints, so two comparisons that differ in either must not collide on one group.
94	 * @param plan - the arms, environments, repetitions, policy version, and seed to freeze.
95	 * @param thresholds - the resolved statistical choices to freeze with them.
96	 * @param caps - the caps both arms resolve to, in cap evaluation order.
97	 * @returns the SHA-256 hex digest; identical inputs give identical digests.
98	 */
99	export function planDigest(
100	  plan: ExperimentPlan,
101	  thresholds: ExperimentThresholds,
102	  caps: readonly BudgetCap[],
103	): string {
104	  const content = JSON.stringify({
105	    version: EXPERIMENT_PLAN_VERSION,
106	    arms: EXPERIMENT_ARM_ROLES.map(role => [
107	      role,
108	      plan[role].provider,
109	      plan[role].model,
110	      digestedImplementer(armImplementer(plan[role])),
111	      digestedLadder(plan[role].ladder),
112	    ]),
113	    environments: [...plan.environments].sort(),
114	    repetitions: plan.repetitions,
115	    policyVersion: plan.policyVersion ?? null,
116	    seed: plan.seed ?? null,
117	    thresholds: [
118	      thresholds.bootstrapResamples,
119	      thresholds.confidenceLevel,
120	      thresholds.minimumDelta,
121	      thresholds.cellTokenCap,
122	    ],
123	    caps,
124	  })
125	  return createHash('sha256').update(content).digest('hex')
126	}
127	
128	/**
129	 * Whether two arms would run their cells under the same ceilings.
130	 * @param baseline - caps resolved for the baseline arm, in cap evaluation order.
131	 * @param candidate - caps resolved for the candidate arm, in the same order.
132	 * @returns `true` when both lists name the same caps at the same values.
133	 */
134	export function capsAgree(baseline: readonly BudgetCap[], candidate: readonly BudgetCap[]): boolean {
135	  return baseline.length === candidate.length
136	    && baseline.every(([cap, limit], index) => {
137	      // The length check above makes every index of `baseline` an index of
138	      // `candidate`, which the element type does not say.
139	      const [otherCap, otherLimit] = candidate[index] as BudgetCap
140	      return otherCap === cap && otherLimit === limit
141	    })
142	}
143	
144	/**
145	 * Render one arm's caps for a diagnostic.
146	 * @param caps - the caps to render, in cap evaluation order.
147	 * @returns `cap=limit` pairs separated by commas, or `none` for an uncapped arm.
148	 */
149	export function describeCaps(caps: readonly BudgetCap[]): string {
150	  return caps.length === 0 ? 'none' : caps.map(([cap, limit]) => `${cap}=${limit}`).join(', ')
151	}
152	
153	/**
154	 * Stamp `group` one arm's sessions carry.
155	 * @param digest - the frozen plan digest.
156	 * @param role - which arm the group names.
157	 * @returns `experiment-<digest>-<role>`.
158	 */
159	export function experimentGroup(digest: string, role: ExperimentArmRole): string {
160	  return `${EXPERIMENT_GROUP_PREFIX}${digest}-${role}`
161	}
162	
163	/**
164	 * Read a group minted by {@link experimentGroup}.
165	 * @param group - a stamp group from an `environment/run` event.
166	 * @returns the digest and role, or `undefined` for a group outside this package's namespace or malformed inside it.
167	 */
168	export function parseExperimentGroup(group: string): { digest: string; role: ExperimentArmRole } | undefined {
169	  const match = GROUP_PATTERN.exec(group)
170	  if (match === null) return undefined
171	  return { digest: match[1] as string, role: match[2] as ExperimentArmRole }
172	}
173	
174	/**
175	 * Tokens a plan may spend at its per-cell cap: every environment, every
176	 * repetition, on both arms.
177	 * @param plan - the environments and repetitions to project.
178	 * @param cellTokenCap - tokens one cell may spend.
179	 * @returns the projected ceiling the token budget is checked against.
180	 */
181	export function projectedTokens(plan: ExperimentPlan, cellTokenCap: number): number {
182	  return plan.environments.length * plan.repetitions * EXPERIMENT_ARM_ROLES.length * cellTokenCap
183	}

454	  } catch (error) {
455	    const detail = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)
456	    return `: disabled expression does not parse: ${detail}`
457	  }
458	}

460	function collectExpressionPaths(value: unknown, path: string, output: string[]): void {
461	  if (isJsExpr(value)) {
462	    output.push(path)
463	    return
464	  }
465	  if (isUnknownArray(value)) {
466	    for (let index = 0; index < value.length; index++) collectExpressionPaths(value[index], `${path}[${index}]`, output)
467	    return
468	  }
469	  if (!isRecord(value)) return
470	  for (const [key, child] of Object.entries(value)) collectExpressionPaths(child, `${path}.${key}`, output)

2	 * Cordis Loader configuration parsing shared by the configuration gates.
3	 *
4	 * The Loader accepts a `!!js` scalar wherever it interpolates an expression. A
5	 * gate must read the authored text rather than its value, so the tag parses
6	 * into an inert node here and is never evaluated.
7	 */
8	
9	import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
10	import { resolve } from 'node:path'
11	import * as yaml from 'js-yaml'
12	
13	const jsExprType = new yaml.Type('tag:yaml.org,2002:js', {
14	  kind: 'scalar',
15	  resolve: data => typeof data === 'string',
16	  construct: (data: unknown): { __jsExpr: string } => {
17	    if (typeof data !== 'string') throw new TypeError('!!js requires a scalar string')
18	    return { __jsExpr: data }
19	  },
20	})
21	const schema = yaml.JSON_SCHEMA.extend(jsExprType)
22	
23	/**
24	 * Parse one Loader configuration document.
25	 * @param source - YAML document text.
26	 * @returns the parsed document; callers decide whether it is an entry array.
27	 * @throws {yaml.YAMLException} when the document does not parse.
28	 */
29	export function parseCordisDocument(source: string): unknown {
30	  return yaml.load(source, { schema })
31	}
32	
33	/**
34	 * Read and parse one Loader configuration file.
35	 * @param root - repository root the path is relative to.
36	 * @param file - repository-relative configuration path.
37	 * @returns the parsed document; callers decide whether it is an entry array.
38	 */
39	export function loadCordisDocument(root: string, file: string): unknown {
40	  return parseCordisDocument(readFileSync(resolve(root, file), 'utf8'))
41	}
42	
43	/**
44	 * Whether a parsed node is an unevaluated `!!js` expression.
45	 * @param value - any parsed node.
46	 * @returns true when the node carries the expression text.
47	 */
48	export function isJsExpr(value: unknown): value is { __jsExpr: string } {
49	  return isRecord(value) && typeof value.__jsExpr === 'string'
50	}
51	
52	/**
53	 * Whether a parsed node is a mapping (or any other non-null object).
54	 * @param value - any parsed node.
55	 * @returns true when the node has properties to walk.
56	 */
57	export function isRecord(value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> {
58	  return value !== null && typeof value === 'object'
59	}
60	
61	/**
62	 * Whether a parsed node is a sequence.
63	 * @param value - any parsed node.
64	 * @returns true when the node is an array.
65	 */
66	export function isUnknownArray(value: unknown): value is unknown[] {
67	  return Array.isArray(value)
68	}

content.content:
## Service contract

`ctx.environmentRuns.run({ environment, workspace, implementer?, model?, ladder?, repetition?, group?, district?, policyVersion?, seed?, signal? })` returns the stamp, one entry per attempt with the route that attempt ran on, the certificate when a run passed, the accumulated `usage`, and the `caps` the cell ran under. It reads the definition from the registry, overlays `task.fixture` (an existing absolute directory) onto `workspace` and hashes its files, and creates a fresh agent with `meta.cwd = workspace`, the requested `model` route or the composition's default selection, and the model-selection setup the headless bundle uses. Before anything else enters the log it appends the `environment/run` stamp: environment id and kind, `heldOut`, the content hashes of prompt, fixture, and checks, `repetition` (default `0`), `group`, and `district`, the `policyVersion` and `seed` the run asked for, the model route, the configured isolation, and the `implementer` name. It then creates the goal from the task prompt, disarms it so a composed goal-round driver never continues it, and authors the standard from the environment's checks verbatim.

With a barrier composed, the run also denies the cell the directory its workspace sits in — `dirname(workspace)` — for the length of the run, through `ctx.readBarrier.denyFor`, and disposes that registration when the run ends. A fleet lays each cell's workspace out as a sibling under the run directory, so that one denial covers the run's plan and log and every other cell at once; naming each sibling instead would leave the run directory itself listable, which states the experiment the cell is part of. The barrier grants the session's own workspace beneath the denial, so the cell reads and writes its own files unchanged. Without a composed barrier nothing is denied, which is what an `isolation: none` claim already says.

With a barrier composed, the run reserves `<barrier root>/runs/<sessionId>/` before the stamp, copies a held-out environment's fixture to `fixture/` and any [declared reference](#the-staged-reference) to `reference/` there, and rewrites each attempt's check command to source a script the reservation holds. The reservation is stocked before the implementer's first turn and again at each attempt with `standard.json` and one `checks/<checkId>/` directory per active check, holding its `run` script and, for a check that carries cases, the `cases.jsonl` those cases live in — so the implementer sees a command line naming a file whose content the barrier denies it. A check id that is not a single path segment, and a reservation path the check command line cannot carry unquoted, both fail the run with `ENVIRONMENT_RUN_UNSAFE_CHECK_SCRIPT`.

Each attempt hands the prompt to the implementer and waits for its work to end, then [digests the check-owned set](#tamper-on-check-owned-paths), copies every `task.immutable` path from the fixture onto the workspace again so implementer edits to validator-owned files never reach the checks while every other file stays as the implementer left it, digests the workspace files, and executes every active check of the current standard through `ctx.shell` with `workdir: workspace`. A check without cases runs once: exit code `0` without timeout or abort is `pass`, anything else `fail`; evidence is the exit fact followed by the bounded tails of stdout and stderr. A check with cases runs [once per case](#weighted-cases-and-the-reservation). `recordRun` records the run under `{ executor: 'runner', treeHash }` — one durable `verification/run` event per attempt, passing or failing, carrying `parity` when any check had cases — and commits a certificate or returns the failing subset. Certified: the goal is completed, which the verification guard admits. Not certified: one [directive](#the-clustered-directive) is recorded, and while attempts remain the next turn carries it in a `<validation_failed>` block.

## The attempt ladder

`ladder` names one rung per attempt, in attempt order: attempt `i` runs on `ladder[i - 1].model`, and a rung that names no model runs the request's own `model`. Present, the ladder's length is the run's attempt bound and overrides the composition's `maxAttempts`, because the caller that chose a model per attempt is the caller that chose how many attempts there are. `resolveLadder(ladder, model, maxRungs)` is the exported resolution step; an empty ladder and one past `maxLadderRungs` both fail with `ENVIRONMENT_RUN_INVALID_LADDER` before an agent exists.

The stamp records the ladder beside `model`, which stays the first attempt's route, so a fold that groups by route alone still sees where the run started while a fold that groups by the arm sees the whole escalation. Every `EnvironmentRunAttempt` states the `model` it ran on and the `transcript` it ran under. A route implementer changes route through the model selection the runner installed on the cell agent, applied before the attempt's first step; a delegated one starts its child on the rung's model id, because a provider names its own models and the rung's harness `provider` is a fact about the route rather than an argument the provider takes.

Model-visible and logged stay equivalent: what the model is asked to be is the request header of every step, which the cell session already logs, and the attempt record and the stamp state what was asked for, never what a provider ran. A delegated attempt's `environment/delegation` carries the child's `reportedModel` for the same reason.

=== FLEET ===
The service requires `environments`, `environmentRuns`, and `agentDefaultModel`. `resolveConfig(config)` is the exported defaulting step.

## Service contract

`ctx.fleet.run(plan)` takes `environments` (`{ ids }` in the given order, or `{ filter }` resolved against the registry in registration order), `models` (an empty list runs the composition's default route from `agentDefaultModel`) that each cell's FIRST attempt runs on, an optional `ladder` of one rung per attempt, an optional `implementer` every cell is run by, a positive integer `repetitions`, an optional exact `cells` selection, an existing absolute `workspaceRoot`, an optional `group`, an optional `district`, an optional `policyVersion`, an optional base `seed`, an optional positive integer `tokenCeiling`, and an optional `signal`. It rejects with `FleetError` before running any cell: `FLEET_INVALID_PLAN` for a non-positive or fractional `repetitions` or `tokenCeiling`, a `seed` that is not a safe non-negative integer, a `ladder` with no rung, an id the registry does not hold, or a `cells` selection that is empty or names a cell the plan does not enumerate; `FLEET_EMPTY_PLAN` when the environment selection matches nothing.

## Policy version and the base seed

`policyVersion` names the checkpoint or policy the plan's routes serve; every cell's run stamp carries it verbatim, so a fold can key measured difficulty by it. `seed` is the plan's **base** seed and each cell runs with `seed + repetition`, so one repetition index means one seed across every route and every environment of the plan — which is what lets a paired design compare like with like. The base is validated once, at the plan boundary, because the arithmetic is the fleet's: a base the runner would refuse must not surface as every cell failing separately. A seed records what a run asked for, never what a provider did with it; the [runner README](../environment-runner/README.md#sampling-and-what-a-replay-reproduces) owns what a replay can and cannot reproduce.

Cells are enumerated environment-major, then model, then repetition from `0`, and run through `ctx.environmentRuns.run` with at most `maxConcurrent` in flight. A plan that names `cells` runs only those, still in plan order, so a driver resuming a partly run plan keeps every cell's environment, route, and repetition index instead of restating them as a smaller plan whose repetition indexes would start again at zero. `fleetCellKey(cell)` is the identity a consumer indexes cells by, inside the ledger it keeps or against the run stamps already in the session logs. Each cell gets a fresh `cell-*` directory under `workspaceRoot` and carries the plan's `group` (or a minted `fleet-<uuid>`), its repetition index, and the plan's `district` into the run stamp, so every session of the batch is grouped durably in its own log. Every cell workspace is a sibling of every other under `workspaceRoot`, beside whatever the driver writes there, so the runner denies each cell everything above its own workspace for the length of its run ([`dsh-environment-runner`](../environment-runner/README.md)). A cell whose run throws is kept as `{ cell, error }` with the harness error code when the error had one; the fleet run itself never fails because of one cell.

Two conditions refuse a cell before it starts, so every plan keeps a row for every cell and the runs and errors columns stay honest. Once one model route has produced `routeBreaker.consecutiveErrors` error outcomes in a row, its remaining cells are recorded as `FLEET_ROUTE_BREAKER_OPEN` errors naming the route and the count; a reported cell resets that route's count, and the breaker is per plan. Once the reports in hand sum past `tokenCeiling` input plus output tokens, every cell that has not started is recorded as a `FLEET_TOKEN_CEILING_REACHED` error, while the cells already in flight complete. A refused cell mints no workspace and folds into neither the breaker nor the spend.

`ladder` is forwarded verbatim to every cell, so one plan is one ladder: attempt `i` of every cell runs on `ladder[i - 1].model` or on the cell's own route when that rung names none, and the ladder's length is each cell's attempt bound. The rung ceiling belongs to the runner's config, so a ladder longer than it fails each cell rather than the plan; only a ladder with no rung at all is refused here, once, because that one is arithmetic no cell could complete. The [runner README](../environment-runner/README.md#the-attempt-ladder) owns what a rung means and how each implementer changes route.

`implementer` is forwarded verbatim to every cell, so one plan is one implementer and the row folded from it never mixes two: `{ kind: 'route' }` (the default) runs each cell on its own model route, while `{ kind: 'subagent', provider, label? }` delegates every attempt of every cell to that registered subagent provider. The [runner README](../environment-runner/README.md#the-two-implementers) owns what a delegated certificate proves and which providers an isolation claim above `none` refuses.

The report carries the `group`, every cell outcome in plan order, the `spend` (`inputTokens` and `outputTokens` of the whole run), and the `leaderboard`: per model route and environment, the environment kind and `heldOut` flag, the `ladder` the runs escalated over, the `isolation` the runs declared and the `implementer` they were stamped with (all three absent when every cell of the row failed before a run, and the ladder also absent for a plan that named none), `runs`, `errors`, `certified`, `certificateRate`, `attemptsMean`, and the summed `inputTokens` and `outputTokens`. `leaderboardMarkdown(report)` renders the same rows as one Markdown table for people; the report stays the record and the session logs stay the authority.

Workspace retention runs once a cell's outcome is in hand: `remove-certified` removes the `cell-*` directory of a cell whose run certified, `remove-all` removes it whether the cell reported or failed, and `keep` removes nothing.

## The `fleet/cell` event

Right after a cell's outcome is recorded and its retention has run, the fleet emits the observe-only Cordis event `fleet/cell` with the plan's `group`, its `district` when it has one, the `cell`, and an `outcome` of `reported` with the runner's `sessionId` and `certified` flag or `error` with the failing code and message. One event per cell, in settle order — which equals plan order only while `maxConcurrent` is `1`. A listener cannot change the outcome and its failure is contained, so an observer such as [the shift driver](../shifts/README.md) writes its own per-cell record without holding this report; the [Cordis catalog](../../../docs/subsystems/improvement.md#cordis-surface) carries the declaration.

## Model Experience
=== EXPERIMENTS ===
The service requires `environments` and `fleet`. `resolveConfig(config)` is the exported defaulting step; it returns the four `thresholds` the plan digest freezes beside the `tokenBudget`, which stays outside the digest because it bounds what a deployment pays for rather than what the comparison measures.

## Service contract

`ctx.experiments.run(plan)` takes `environments` (registered ids, each named once), a positive integer `repetitions`, the `baseline` and `candidate` arms, an existing absolute `workspaceRoot`, and optionally a `policyVersion` both arms' routes serve, a base `seed`, a `digest` the caller froze earlier, a `signal`, and a `sink`.

Each arm is a model route — `provider` and `model` — its first attempt runs on, an optional `ladder` of one rung per attempt, and an optional `implementer`, the same values a fleet plan takes: `{ kind: 'route' }`, which an arm naming none runs, has every attempt of every cell of that arm driven on the arm's own route, while `{ kind: 'subagent', provider, label? }` delegates each attempt to that registered subagent provider. The [runner README](../environment-runner/README.md#the-two-implementers) owns what a delegated certificate proves and which providers an isolation claim above `none` refuses. Nothing here re-validates the provider: an implementer the composition cannot honor fails every cell of its arm through the runner, so every repetition of that arm goes unpaired and the verdict is `inconclusive`.

An arm's `ladder` is the same list a fleet plan takes and rides through to every cell of that arm, and its first rung is the arm's own route: it either names no model, or names exactly the arm's `provider` and `model`. A first rung naming another route is refused with `EXPERIMENT_LADDER_CONFLICT`, because the arm is what the result and every scoreboard row are published under and a first attempt on another route would publish that identity over a route it never ran. The rest of the rungs are free, which is what a cheap-then-strong or a downshift arm is.

It rejects with `ExperimentError` before running any cell: `EXPERIMENT_INVALID_PLAN` for a non-positive or fractional `repetitions`, a `seed` that is not a safe non-negative integer, an empty environment list, an arm ladder with no rung, an id named twice, or an id the registry does not hold; `EXPERIMENT_LADDER_CONFLICT` when an arm's first rung names a route other than the arm's own; `EXPERIMENT_UNEQUAL_CAPS` when the two arms would run their cells under different caps; `EXPERIMENT_PLAN_NOT_FROZEN` when a declared `digest` differs from the recomputed one; `EXPERIMENT_OVER_BUDGET` when `environments × repetitions × 2 × cellTokenCap` exceeds `tokenBudget`.

Both arms are forwarded the same `policyVersion` and the same base `seed`, and each arm's cell samples with `seed + repetition`, so the paired repetitions of the two arms differ only in the arm itself, its route and its implementer — the [fleet README](../fleet/README.md#policy-version-and-the-base-seed) owns the arithmetic and the [runner README](../environment-runner/README.md#sampling-and-what-a-replay-reproduces) what a replay reproduces.

Both arms then run as two `ctx.fleet.run` calls over the same ids at the same repetition count, baseline first, each carrying its own arm's route and implementer. A cell the fleet kept as an error leaves its repetition unpaired rather than failing the experiment. The result is written to `sink` as one JSON line and the sink is closed exactly once; the sink is the trajectory exporter's `TrajectorySink`, so `jsonlFileSink(path)` from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-trajectories` serves both exports.

The result restates each arm beside its stamp group: `arms.baseline` and `arms.candidate` carry the `model` route, the `ladder` the arm escalated over when it named one, and the `implementer` the arm ran under, with an omitted implementer stated as `{ kind: 'route' }`, so a stored result tells a harness-native arm from a delegated one without the plan that produced it. `caps` states the ceilings every cell of both arms ran under, in cap evaluation order, so a reader of a stored result sees the budget the comparison was measured inside without finding the composition behind it.

### The arms run under one budget

A cell stopped at one wall or token ceiling measures something different from the same cell stopped at another, so two arms bounded differently compare the ceilings as much as the arms. `ctx.environmentRuns.cellCaps` answers what one cell of an arm runs under — [the runner README](../environment-runner/README.md#the-budget-a-delegated-attempt-runs-under) owns how a delegated cell is bounded and which cap it can lose — and a plan whose two arms resolve to different lists is refused with `EXPERIMENT_UNEQUAL_CAPS` before either arm starts. The refusal spends nothing, which is the point: the arms would otherwise run in full to produce a comparison a reader must then discount.

`foldExperiment(request)` is the pure fold behind the run and is exported for tests and offline tools, together with `planDigest`, `capsAgree`, `describeCaps`, `experimentGroup`, `ladderConflicts`, `parseExperimentGroup`, `projectedTokens`, `EXPERIMENT_ARM_ROLES`, `EXPERIMENT_GROUP_PREFIX`, and the `bootstrapIntervals` pass.

## Freezing and the group scheme

`planDigest(plan, thresholds, caps)` is the SHA-256 hex digest over a format version, the two arms in role order — each its model route, its implementer, and its attempt ladder — the environment ids **sorted**, the repetition count, the `policyVersion` and base `seed`, the four thresholds, and the caps both arms agreed on. Sorting makes the digest independent of the order a caller listed the ids in; the workspace root, the abort signal, and the sink are not digested because they change nothing the comparison measures. The policy version and the seed are digested because both arms' sessions are found in the logs by the groups the digest mints, so two comparisons that differ in either must not collide on one group. The caps are digested because they decide when a cell stops; the deployment's `tokenBudget` stays outside, because it bounds what a deployment pays for across plans rather than what one comparison measures.

An arm's implementer enters the digest as the default `{ kind: 'route' }` when the arm names none, so a plan that omits the field and one that spells it out are one experiment; a delegated arm digests its subagent provider and label, in fixed positions that the key order a caller wrote cannot change. Which arm delegates is part of the identity, because the roles are digested in order. An arm's ladder digests one entry per rung, with `null` for a rung that names no model, so two arms that escalate differently are two experiments while a plan that ladders nothing digests as it always did.

1	# Agent Note: Program workflow integrity — a certificate over a commit, a confined integration, and an integration that resumes
2	
3	Status: proposed
4	
5	English | [中文](2026-09-08-program-workflow-integrity.zh.md)
6	
7	## Problem
8	
9	The first real program run of [`dsh-program`](../../../../packages/improvement/program/README.md) delivered its release, and the record of it — [`data/proving-ground/2026-09-08-self-assessment-program-artefacts`](../../../../data/proving-ground/2026-09-08-self-assessment-program-artefacts/manifest.json) — needed three operator interventions to get there. Each one is a hole in the workflow rather than a mistake the operator made.
10	
11	**A department was certified over a worktree, and the branch it delivered was empty.** The department wrote `assessment.md`, its checks passed on the files on disk, and the program recorded it `certified`. Nothing it wrote was ever committed, so `git merge --no-ff` of that branch carried nothing and the integration's own check failed with "missing assessment.md". The integration agent then spent 22 steps trying to satisfy a check about a file no branch held, and the operator stopped the run, committed the department's tree by hand, and started the program again. The certificate had claimed a tree; only a commit is delivered.
12	
13	**The integration was unconfined and edited a department's file.** Before that hand commit, the first integration attempt found the department worktree beside its own, and at step 20 it rewrote sentences of `assessment.md` with a python script. The text the department certified at 11:47:50 UTC survives only because the record reconstructs it from the department session's own write and edit calls (`assessment.certified.md`); the file the program released (`assessment.md`) carries the integration agent's edits. An integration that can write into a department worktree makes every department certificate a claim about a tree someone else may have changed since.
14	
15	**The interrupted integration could not be resumed.** `driveIntegration` creates its session at the derived id `departmentSessionId(programId, INTEGRATION_KEY)`. After the operator's restart, `resume()` reached `close()` and then `integrate()`, which created that id a second time, and persistence refused it: `cannot publish session "program-…-@integration": persisted state already owns this identity` ([`resume-refusal.log`](../../../../data/proving-ground/2026-09-08-self-assessment-program-artefacts/resume-refusal.log)). The operator moved the first integration session aside under `sessions-superseded/` to get the program to finish. A program whose integration is killed mid-flight cannot finish without hand-editing the persistence root.
16	
17	## Proposal
18	
19	Three rules, all inside the service that already owns the ledger.
20	
21	**A certificate covers a commit.** `attempts()` reads `git status --porcelain` in the workspace before it runs any check. A non-empty status means the attempt measures nothing: it spends its round, issues a directive whose root cause is `the worktree carries work that no commit on this branch carries`, and hands the session an `<uncommitted_work>` turn listing the porcelain lines and telling it that uncommitted work is not delivered. The round cap bounds those attempts exactly as it bounds failing checks, so a session that never commits ends `failed` instead of certifying something the integration cannot merge. The rule sits in `attempts()` rather than in the department path, so the integration session is held to it over its own worktree too.
22	
23	**The record states what was certified.** A certified department records `revision` (`git rev-parse HEAD`) and `tree` (`git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}`) on its `program/goal`, carried together as one `CertifiedTree` in the run state so neither half can exist without the other. A reconciliation keeps what the ledger recorded and reads the worktree only when the ledger records nothing — a process that died between a department's certificate and the record of it. Before merging, the integration compares each branch head against the recorded revision and refuses a branch that moved, recording `program/integration { failed }` naming both revisions: a department that moved after certification is not what was certified. A branch the integration worktree already contains, which is what an interrupted integration leaves, is skipped through `git merge-base --is-ancestor` rather than merged again.
24	
25	**The integration is sealed like a cell.** When `readBarrier` is composed, `driveIntegration` registers `denyFor(agent.session, <workspaceRoot>/<programId>)` for the length of the integration and disposes it when the integration ends — the same registration the [sealed cell](2026-09-08-sealed-cell-workspace.md) makes for an environment run, and for the same reason. The denied directory is the program's worktrees root: the barrier grants a session its own workspace beneath a denied strict ancestor, and every department worktree is a sibling of the integration's inside that root, so one registration reaches every department worktree and nothing of the integration's own. No per-department denial is added, because the layout `worktreePath` mints makes the parent denial exact. Both closing records carry `denied`, empty for a composition without a barrier, so the log states what the integration could not reach. `isolation` stays `none`: the denial is worth what the composed executors enforce, which is what that claim already says.
26	
27	**An interrupted integration is taken back over.** A pass that reconciles a ledger whose last integration record is `running` and whose integration session persistence already holds resumes that session through `ctx.agents.resume`, resumes its goal, and continues at the attempt after the validation runs its own log records — so the round cap covers the whole integration rather than each process that drove it. The standing `running` record is what the pass owns; no second one is appended, which the package's own invariant does not admit either. A `running` record whose process died before the session existed opens it under that same record, and a session that carries no goal to resume records `failed` with `PROGRAM_INTEGRATION_UNRESUMABLE`.
28	
29	## Alternatives considered
30	
31	**Certify the tree the checks saw, and commit it for the department.** The program would commit whatever the worktree held before recording the certificate. It removes the refusal and the extra round, and it makes the program an author of the deliverable: the branch would then carry a commit no department wrote, made by a service whose whole claim is that it never writes into a worktree. The department is the one that knows what belongs in the commit; the program is the one that can tell it the work is not delivered.
32	
33	**Record the tree digest and let the integration merge whatever the branch points at.** The `tree` alone tells a reader that two certificates delivered the same files, but nothing refuses a branch that moved: the integration would merge the new head and certify a merged revision no department certificate covers. Refusing at the merge is what makes the department record load-bearing.
34	
35	**Deny each department worktree explicitly.** One `denyFor` per department, registered as each certifies, denies the same paths and needs a registration per department kept current while departments are still certifying. The worktrees root is one path known before any session exists, and it also covers whatever else a deployment puts beside the worktrees. Per-department denials would matter under a layout where the integration worktree's parent is not the worktrees root, which `worktreePath` does not mint.
36	
37	**Give the resumed integration a fresh session id.** A suffixed id — `@integration-2` — would let the pass create rather than resume, and it drops the interrupted attempt's own log: the round cap would start over per process, the earlier attempts' runs would be in a session no ledger record names, and "one session per key" would stop being a property of the derived identity. Resuming keeps the id the ledger already published.
38	
39	**Let the integration re-merge every branch and rely on git.** `git merge --no-ff` of an already-merged branch exits zero and merges nothing, so the skip is not needed for correctness. Asking `git merge-base --is-ancestor` states the intent instead of depending on that behaviour, and it keeps a resumed integration's command log free of merges that did nothing.
40	
41	## Acceptance criteria
42	
43	- A department whose worktree is dirty is not certified: the attempt runs no check, the department session's directive names the uncommitted work, and the next turn is an `<uncommitted_work>` block carrying the porcelain lines. Once the department commits, it certifies and the `program/goal` record carries the commit and its tree. A department that never commits ends `failed` on its round cap with no certificate in its log.
44	- The integration refuses a department branch whose head is no longer the recorded revision, records `program/integration { failed }` naming both, and merges nothing; a branch the integration worktree already contains is skipped rather than merged again.
45	- With a read barrier composed, the integration session is denied the program's worktrees root for the length of the integration, the registration is disposed when it ends, and both closing records carry that path in `denied`; a composition without a barrier records an empty list.
46	- Over [`examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/program/`](../../../../examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/program/cordis.yml), a Loader-booted keyless composition runs a program whose departments write before they commit and whose integration repairs a merged head no department branch could satisfy: the integration's `read` of a department worktree file appends one `read-barrier/denied` naming the `fs` capability, the certified department records carry a 40-hex revision and tree, and the released program's merged revision is a commit of the integration's own.
47	- In that same fixture, a boot killed after the integration's first run over the merged head is followed by one that takes the integration back over on the id it already owns: the program releases, its ledger carries exactly one `running` record before the `certified` one, and one `@integration` member session exists.
48	
49	## Risks
50	
51	- **A department that leaves ignored-but-untracked files stalls.** The porcelain status is the whole rule, so build output a check produced and the repository does not ignore reads as uncommitted work and burns the round cap. The deployment's own ignore rules are the only lever; the spec cannot state an exception.
52	- **The seal is only as strong as the executors under it.** `denyFor` binds the capabilities that refuse a read in the operation that opens paths. A deployment composing an unconfined shell beside the barrier leaves that seam able to reach a department worktree — which is exactly what the recorded run did — and the `denied` list on the record will still name the directory. A district that wants the seal enforced composes the sandbox-confined executor the [sealed cell](2026-09-08-sealed-cell-workspace.md) names.
53	- **A moved branch ends the program rather than re-certifying it.** An operator who moves a department branch on purpose — the recovery the recorded run performed — now gets a failed integration instead of a merge. Starting the program again reconciles that department from its own log and certifies the new head, which is a longer path than the operator took, and a truthful one.

# Agent Note: 计划工作流的完整性——证书覆盖提交、被围起来的集成、可恢复的集成

Status: proposed

[English](2026-09-08-program-workflow-integrity.md) | 中文

## Problem

[`dsh-program`](../../../../packages/improvement/program/README.md) 的第一次真实计划运行交付了它的发布，而它的记录——[`data/proving-ground/2026-09-08-self-assessment-program-artefacts`](../../../../data/proving-ground/2026-09-08-self-assessment-program-artefacts/manifest.json)——为此需要三次操作者干预。每一次都是工作流上的一个漏洞，而不是操作者犯的错。

**一个部门在工作树之上被认证，而它交付的分支是空的。** 该部门写了 `assessment.md`，它的检查在磁盘上的文件上通过，计划把它记为 `certified`。它写的任何东西都从未被提交，于是对该分支的 `git merge --no-ff` 什么也没带过来，集成自己的检查以 "missing assessment.md" 失败。随后集成 agent 花了 22 步试图满足一个关于任何分支都不持有的文件的检查，操作者停下运行、手工提交了该部门的工作树，并重新启动了计划。证书宣称的是一棵树；而被交付的只有提交。

**集成没有被围起来，并改写了某个部门的文件。** 在那次手工提交之前，第一次集成尝试在自己的工作树旁边找到了部门工作树，并在第 20 步用一个 python 脚本改写了 `assessment.md` 的若干句子。该部门在 UTC 11:47:50 认证的文本之所以留存，只是因为记录从部门会话自身的写入与编辑调用中重建了它（`assessment.certified.md`）；计划发布的文件（`assessment.md`）携带的是集成 agent 的编辑。一个能写入部门工作树的集成，会把每一份部门证书变成对一棵别人此后可能改动过的树的宣称。

**被中断的集成无法恢复。** `driveIntegration` 在派生 id `departmentSessionId(programId, INTEGRATION_KEY)` 上创建它的会话。在操作者重启后，`resume()` 到达 `close()`、继而 `integrate()`，后者第二次创建了那个 id，而持久化拒绝了它：`cannot publish session "program-…-@integration": persisted state already owns this identity`（[`resume-refusal.log`](../../../../data/proving-ground/2026-09-08-self-assessment-program-artefacts/resume-refusal.log)）。操作者把第一个集成会话挪到 `sessions-superseded/` 之下，才让计划得以完成。一个集成被中途杀死的计划，不手工编辑持久化根目录就无法完成。

## Proposal

三条规则，全部落在已经拥有账本的那个服务里。

# POC overlay: keep the advanced headless agent and model-facing tools, but
# place its filesystem and process substrate in one short-lived E2B sandbox;
# the generic Bash, PTY, and LSP consumers compose above them.
#
# One-world invariant: e2b.cwd, sandbox-policy.workspaceRoot, and bash-local's
# default workdir (implicit host process.cwd()) must all name the same remote
# directory. Only e2b.cwd is created at sandbox open; dropping its !!js line
# falls back to /home/user/workspace while Bash and PTY keep targeting the
# host path, so every tool call fails with a remote spawn error.
- id: base
  name: '@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-include'
  config:
    path: ./advanced.cordis.yml
    patches:
      - id: subprocess
        name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subprocess-local'
        disabled: true
      - id: fs-local
        name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-local'
        disabled: true
      - insert:
          - id: e2b
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-e2b'
            config:
              cwd: !!js process.cwd()
              timeoutMs: 300000
          - id: subprocess-e2b
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subprocess-e2b'
          - id: fs-e2b
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-e2b'
          - id: sandbox-policy
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-policy'
            config:
              mode: danger-full-access
              workspaceRoot: !!js process.cwd()
          - id: pty
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-terminal'
          - id: terminal-bash
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-terminal-bash'
          - id: tool-terminal
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-terminal'
          - id: lsp
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-lsp'
          - id: lsp-stdio
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-lsp-stdio'
            config:
              servers:
                typescript:
                  command: npx
                  args: [--yes, typescript-language-server@5.0.0, --stdio]
                  extensionToLanguage:
                    .ts: typescript
                    .tsx: typescriptreact
                    .js: javascript
                    .jsx: javascriptreact
          - id: tool-lsp
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-lsp'

# One-shot coding agent with format-pure stdout. The app bin loads the
# gitignored root `.env` into the process environment; entry configs here are
# the composition base, while user-plane values resolve per request through
# the two providers below.

# User-settings document (`$DSH_HOME/settings.yaml`, hot-reloaded): a
# `llm-deepseek:` section there overrides the adapter entry below without a
# restart.
- id: settings
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-settings-file'

# Credential store: the live process environment over `$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml`
# (owner-only file, hot-reloaded). The adapter resolves `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`
# through it at each request, so no key is inlined in this file.
- id: credentials
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-credentials-local'

# The DeepSeek adapter. Swap to '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai' for the pi-ai-backed
# twin (a `providers` dict keyed by route; `reasoning: high` replaces
# thinking/reasoningEffort). Shipped default: full thinking at max effort on
# every request. Exact-model resolution materializes request defaults before
# the request header is logged.
- id: llm-deepseek
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-deepseek'
  config:
    thinking: enabled
    reasoningEffort: max
    models:
      - id: deepseek-v4-pro
        contextWindow: 128000
      - id: deepseek-v4-flash
        contextWindow: 128000

# Managed child-process groups for the bash executor (spawn/kill/output plumbing).
- id: subprocess
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subprocess-local'

- id: bash
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-bash-local'
  config:
    timeoutMs: 60000

- id: agent-spine
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-spine-demo'
  config:

        # Stays on flash: the goal/ralph replay corpora were recorded on it, and
        # their nested-include overlays cannot re-pin the app config (a config
        # patch cannot target an entry behind a nested include).
        model: deepseek-v4-flash
        cwd: !!js process.cwd()
    workspaceContext:
      maxBytes: 65536
    persona: |
      You are headless-agent, a coding assistant powered by the {{model}} model.

      Verify your work by running the code or tests. Keep answers brief and
      factual.

  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence-jsonl'
  config:
    root: './.sessions'
    compression: !!js "process.env.DSH_SNAPSHOT === undefined ? 'zstd' : 'none'"

  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-checkpoint-policy'

  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-token-meter'

  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-basic'

    thresholdRatio: 0.8

[package.json](package.json) declares the packages loaded by those configs, while each leaf's private `package.json` remains metadata only.

45:### Name the role that exists
46-
47-Name the stable current responsibility. Do not name the first implementation, a possible future expansion, or the Cordis base class. An interface package names the capability. An implementation package adds the mechanism, protocol, environment, or vendor that distinguishes it. Use `local` only when same-host execution is part of the contract.
48-
49-Use a singular `ctx` key for one engine, runtime, policy, controller, resolver, store, or current configuration. Use a plural key for a registry or a service that owns multiple named members. The class role and key number must agree. Do not reuse one Cordis `Context` key for incompatible host and client declarations. TypeScript declaration merging sees both faces even when they use separate runtime contexts. Add the role suffix when the natural plural already belongs to another face.
50-
51-| Word | Use it when | Do not use it when |
52-|---|---|---|
53-| `Controller` | It accepts commands or user intent and changes one existing domain or presentation state. | It executes arbitrary work, owns a provider fleet, or only converts values for display. |
54-| `Store` | It owns one data set and mainly offers CRUD, snapshot, or subscription operations for that data. | It validates a state machine, arbitrates authority, dispatches work, or owns provider precedence. A map does not make a class a store. |
55-| `Directory` | It exposes entries and metadata for discovery or selection. | Producers register arbitrary implementations into it, or callers execute work through it. |
56-| `Presenter` | It is a pure conversion from domain values or tool arguments to render intent. | It performs I/O, subscribes, mutates state, or owns lifecycle. |
57-| `Registry` | It owns a dynamic set of named registrations, including lookup, duplicate or precedence rules, lifetime, and disposal. | Its main contract is dispatch, execution, cancellation, policy, or orchestration. |
58-| `Runtime` | It runs live work and owns dispatch, cancellation, provider coordination, or operation lifecycle across calls. | It only stores records, returns a catalog, resolves one value, or holds configuration. |
59-| `Resolver` | It computes or locates one answer from supplied inputs without owning that answer's lifecycle. | It owns a mutable collection or long-running execution. |
60-| `Binder` | It attaches one declared interface to a caller context or lifecycle and returns the bound value. | It owns the value as a collection, controls its domain state, or only converts data. |
61-| `Engine` | It implements a domain algorithm or stateful execution model. | It only selects a provider or forwards across a protocol boundary. |
62-| `Policy` | It decides what is allowed, selected, limited, or observed. | It performs the mechanism that the decision permits. |
63-| `Executor` | It runs one explicit request or resolved specification in one capability. | It owns a broad application lifecycle or provider catalog. |
64-| `Gateway` | It adapts a process, network, RPC, or API boundary. | It only registers same-process services or stores metadata. |
65-| `Provider` | It supplies one implementation of a capability definition. Add a mechanism or vendor qualifier when several can exist. | It is the capability definition, provider registry, or consumer runtime. |

/**
   * Refuse the plan's implementer before any cell of it is enumerated. A
   * provider the composition cannot honor refuses every cell it is given, so
   * without this the whole plan runs as a plan of errors and its leaderboard
   * reports rows nothing ran; the runner's own refusal names the provider once
   * instead, before a workspace exists.
   *
   * The stamped route of a laddered plan is its first rung's model, which is
   * what the runner stamps and what a delegated cell's first child is started
   * on; a rung naming none, and a plan without a ladder, stamp the cell's own
   * route. Every route the plan names is checked, because a plan compares
   * routes and one provider may accept some and not others.
   * @param plan - the plan being validated.
   * @param models - the routes the plan's cells run on, already defaulted.
   * @throws {@link EnvironmentRunError} for a provider the composition does not
   *   hold, cannot confine under its isolation, cannot tell which model to run,
   *   or has no budget policy to bound.
   */
  private checkImplementer(plan: FleetPlan, models: readonly EnvironmentRunModel[]): void {
    const implementer = plan.implementer ?? { kind: 'route' }
    for (const model of models) {
      this.ctx.environmentRuns.checkImplementer(implementer, plan.ladder?.[0]?.model ?? model)
    }
  }
